pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Add EATT channel option flag
pr_body:
Adds an option flag to the `bt_gatt_*_params` structs if EATT is enabled so that the application can choose to send a request/indication/notification over enhanced channels, the unenhanced channel or any ATT channel. This is an implementation of the previously posted RFC https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/41909.

Usages in the tree are updated to use `BT_ATT_CHAN_ANY` which keeps the current behavior.

The option is not added for the write command, as it does not have a parameter struct. We should consider adding this and replacing the current functions that takes the parameters individually.

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/41355

I would like to get this merged before RC1 tomorrow and there are only two small issues remaining that we need to reach consensus on.

- The name of the channel selection field/enum.
  - We need to choose between "option", "preference", "flags", "opts". I am fine with any of these.
- What values should the different enumerations have?
  - We want the value `0x0` to keep the old behaviour, ie. any ATT channel can be used.
  - We want to be able to require that only enhanced or unenhanced channels are used, so two bits are used for this.
  - Do we allow the value `0x3` to mean "any", the same as `0x0`? I would say yes, as it would be unintuitive behaviour for the bit field otherwise.

My 2 cents:
We want to _ensure_ that a GATT request is sent on an EATT channel (requirement from the higher layer profile HAP). To me that indicates that this is not a _preference_, as preference indicates something that my be overwritten by e.g. the stack. 

In `bluetooth.h` we have `BT_LE_SCAN_OPT_*`, `BT_LE_ADV_OPT_*`, `BT_LE_PER_ADV_OPT_*`, `BT_LE_PER_ADV_SYNC_OPT_*` and `BT_LE_PER_ADV_SYNC_TRANSFER_OPT_*` that are also bitfields of options for a specific instance of something. I think it makes sense to continue that naming scheme. 
In these options we also have a few options that are mutually exclusive, so I personally think that having

```c
	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_NONE = 0x0,
	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_UNENHANCED_ONLY = BIT(0),
	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_ENHANCED_ONLY = BIT(1),
```
Would be the right solution as 
1) 0x00 retains the current behavior
2) We can _ensure_ that something is sent over a specific type of channel (EATT vs ATT)
3) It is expandable. 
4) We can easily document (and verify) that `BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_UNENHANCED_ONLY` and `BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_ENHANCED_ONLY` are mutually exclusive

Without a use case for ATT-only, it could also be shortened to 
```c
	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_NONE = 0x0,
	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_ENHANCED_ONLY = BIT(0),
```

> Without a use case for ATT-only, it could also be shortened to
>
>	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_NONE = 0x0,
>	BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_ENHANCED_ONLY = BIT(0),

I think this is sufficient for "real" applications. This sidesteps the issue with enhanced and unenhanced bits being mutually exclusive.

The use for testing may be figured out later, potentially having the bit for unenhanced only available during testing.

> We can easily document (and verify) that BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_UNENHANCED_ONLY and BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_ENHANCED_ONLY are mutually exclusive

This is the current behavior, setting both is not allowed. Not well documented though.

> > We can easily document (and verify) that BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_UNENHANCED_ONLY and BT_ATT_CHAN_OPT_ENHANCED_ONLY are mutually exclusive
> 
> This is the current behavior, setting both is not allowed. Not well documented though.

Right. I also think that the suffix `_ONLY` also makes it clearer that this is an exclusive option.

>  I also think that the suffix _ONLY also makes it clearer that this is an exclusive option.

Agree

Guys be warned that if you do add such option for marking request to only be sent by certain bearer type you will either have to reorder the att->tx_queue or with the current implementation risk adding delays processing it since no channel with the required type may be available the requests needs to be push back until it can be sent blocking the entire queue, the only procedures that don't suffer from these problems are notification and write command since they are not queued one can just have a flag e.g. reliable, which is actually what really matters here since the spec requiring EATT are probably doing it for reliability and not exactly because of being EATT per se, in fact if another bearer were to be introduced with similar guaranties these option would immediately become obsolete.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: API to determine if notification over EATT is possible
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The Hearing Aid Service (HAS) has a requirement that if sending notification over EATT is possible, then we shall send a notification over EATT, else indication over ATT. 

Currently Zephyr have no way of exposing this information to the upper layers, nor any way for the upper layers to determine this themselves. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Possible solutions:
A) Add API to enforce usage of EATT, and return error if not possible (upper layer can then switch to indication)
B) Add API to check if EATT channel is available, and then upper layer can choose course of action based on this

Other solutions may also be considered.
comments: Besides checking for client support, we will also need a way to enforce the ATT layer to use an enhanced bearer.
@alwa-nordic and others will take over the implementation and change of EATT.

review_comments: Should this also be guarded by `#if defined(CONFIG_BT_EATT)`?
We would save some space at the cost of having some more `#if defined(CONFIG_BT_EATT)` in some places.
It's not a huge deal anyways, so I am fine with leaving it as is.

this seems to be adressing luiz' comment. Do we have a babblesim testcase where we actually test it? Could we have one if not? Doesn't necessarily have to be part of this PR since you seem to have a verification PR opened too.
I will add some more testing.

Btw, it is also possible to provide arguments when starting a test using the `-argstest` argument. It will basically provide the same as this, so there's no need to modify anything, but it could be a way of just having a single main function and a single test_id, by providing the `chan_opt` as a argument to the test.
I would prefer this as well, also is it possible to only have one .sh file running each vector, instead of each vector being a different script?

I added a .sh file for each so that they can run in parallel and are automatically found by the `run_parallell.sh` script.

Also, we probably don't need all the combinations. (`none_*` and `*_none` should be sufficient.)

What we have done some of the other places, is that we have a `_<name>.sh` file (which isn't picked up by CI) to run all the tests locally like here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/d4dfb68ee5b083c8db87b9bd5db37041435726b5/tests/bluetooth/bsim_bt/bsim_test_audio/test_scripts/_cap.sh

edit: same comment for `att_req_send_process`
Yes, should be `prev->flags` instead of `chan->flags` twice.
since enums don't have a type, should we pack the definition? Do you know what we usually do @Thalley ?
You mean to ensure that `sizeof(enum bt_att_chan_opt) == 1`? We could do that. I also see we set the `-fshort-enums` for the bsim board and armclang/clang compilers.

If we expect `enum`s to have a specific size, then we should pack it. I don't think we need to pack it here though, as the `chan_opt` isn't a value that we need to send over air or anything. 

But in general we do not pack `enum`s in the public API
